prompt: In a new chat, the assistant has no idea what you discussed yesterday.
tells: has no idea what you discussed yesterday
why: Each request starts fresh; nothing is remembered unless the app sends it again. The model has no memory between calls.
trap: The window wasn't overflowing; the old chat was never sent.

prompt: The chat app sends the whole conversation so far with every new message.
tells: sends the whole conversation so far with every new message
why: Because the model keeps no memory, the app resends the history each time to make it look continuous.
trap: This uses up the window, but the reason it happens is that the model is stateless.

prompt: The app's 'memory' feature saves facts about you and adds them to each new prompt.
tells: adds them to each new prompt
why: Memory has to be added by the app because the model itself starts fresh every call.
trap: It's stored by the app and inserted; the model still remembers nothing.

prompt: Each API call is answered on its own, with no link to the call before it.
tells: with no link to the call before it
why: The model treats every request independently. That's having no memory between calls.
trap: It's about the API's requests, not about tools the model calls.

prompt: The developer forgot to include earlier messages, so the bot kept asking the user's name again.
why: Without the earlier messages, the model can't know what was said. It doesn't keep memory on its own.
trap: Nothing was too long; the history just wasn't sent.

prompt: Correcting the chatbot today doesn't change how it answers other users tomorrow.
tells: doesn't change how it answers other users tomorrow
why: Chatting doesn't retrain the model; each call starts from the same fixed model. It has no memory across calls.
trap: Its knowledge is fixed at training, but the clue is that conversations don't carry over.
